pathways.title: Curriculum Module: Student Pathways & Subject Selection Guide 26-27

essentials.title: Meet the Principal for your weekly academic leadership meeting
essentials.description: Use the meeting to review how implementation is going and follow up the actions you agreed last time. Keep minutes with named owners and deadlines.

source.quote: Principal - Academic Coordinator meeting: weekly school academic leadership, implementation review, and follow-up.

essentials.title: Check pacing across classes and subjects
essentials.description: Between the EASE Weeks this is the ordinary work of the role. Look for classes that are falling behind, big gaps between classes in the same subject, and Common Assessment entries that are missing rather than low.

source.quote: Look for classes more than a chapter behind, subjects where one class is far ahead of another

essentials.title: Carry out your share of formal classroom observations
essentials.description: You are one of the school's own appraisers, so your formal observations count towards the teacher's F2 score. Record each one in Edunav and hold the Glow / Grow / Go conversation straight after the lesson.
essentials.timing_text: Throughout each semester, following the observation split you agreed

source.quote: Observe teachers as one of your school's own appraisers, and record it in Edunav

essentials.title: Look over the shared homework calendar
essentials.description: Check the homework calendar in Edunav so that students do not get too many core-subject assignments on the same day. Speak to the teachers concerned when deadlines pile up.
essentials.timing_text: Weekly (the Assessment Policy gives this as its example)

source.quote: with the SL/Academic Coordinator reviewing weekly to ensure no more than 2 core-subject assignments land on the same day

essentials.title: Escalate subject gaps and implementation risks early
essentials.description: Raise a problem while there is still time to fix it: Subject Teacher → Academic Coordinator → Subject Specialist → Academic Board. Never solve it by quietly dropping Cambridge content or changing weightings.

source.quote: Escalates subject gaps and implementation risks early.

tasks.title: Confirm subject groups and class placements
tasks.description: Before teaching starts, check which subject groups will run and which class each student sits in, against the grade-band structures and your school's placement decisions.
tasks.timing_text: First week of each semester

source.quote: Confirm subject group offerings and class placements against the Curriculum Module's grade-band structures

tasks.title: Build your assessment and tracking calendar for the semester
tasks.description: Put the semester's two EASE Weeks and the Teacher-Paced Test timing from the Annual Plan on one calendar, then work backwards from each one. A Synchronized Test week that arrives as a surprise is a week of lost teaching.
tasks.timing_text: In the first two weeks of each semester

source.quote: Build your own tracking calendar for the whole semester in your first two weeks.

tasks.title: Agree who observes whom this semester
tasks.description: Agree the split of formal observations with the Principal and the Subject Leaders, so every teacher in the Teacher Appraisal population is covered and nobody is observed five times by accident. Teachers still in Teacher Induction are not on the F2 schedule.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: agree at the start of each semester how the required observations are shared between you, the Principal, and the Subject Leaders

tasks.title: Run the School Curriculum Implementation Checklist
tasks.description: Check protected curriculum time, schemes of work, assessment load, student transitions and evidence. Close with the four review questions: are we teaching it, are students learning it, where is delivery at risk, and what action will close the gap?
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester and again at mid-semester

source.quote: Use once at the start of each semester and review at mid-semester.

tasks.title: Check current external exam and admissions dates
tasks.description: Re-check the official provider and government sources (Cambridge, TKA, SNPMB/UTBK, SAT, IELTS where relevant) before you counsel students or send any date to families. Never copy a date from last year's document.
tasks.timing_text: Before Grade 12 Semester I and before Grade 11 counselling begins

source.quote: Before the start of Grade 11 counseling and again before Grade 12 Semester I, the Academic Coordinator checks each external provider relevant to their students.

tasks.title: Run the placement test for new Grade 9 and Grade 10 students
tasks.description: Test content and English level, then place each new student in the Intensive or Regular class from the evidence. A parent request or the school of origin alone is not a placement criterion.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year, for new students

source.quote: Administer the placement test. Track progress of Intensive Class students each term. Manage class movement decisions.

tasks.title: Tell families which Checkpoint series your school will sit
tasks.description: May is the network default; March or October needs prior Academic Board approval and a check of the current Cambridge deadlines.
tasks.timing_text: Once a year, early in Semester I

source.quote: Your school's Academic Coordinator communicates the approved series to families each year.

tasks.title: Lead the review of last year's Checkpoint results
tasks.description: When the May-series results are released, go through them with the subject teachers: which strands were weak, and what this means for the new Grade 9 classes.
tasks.timing_text: When Cambridge releases the results (May-series results arrive around July)

source.quote: Lead the analysis of Checkpoint results with subject teachers.

tasks.title: Map each Grade 11 student to a university pathway
tasks.description: Record whether each student is on the domestic or the international pathway, and plan only the external tests that pathway actually needs.
tasks.timing_text: July–August

source.quote: Academic Coordinator maps each student to domestic or international pathway.

tasks.title: Review Grade 10 Intensive Class placements
tasks.description: Use real assessment results and subject-teacher input to decide whether each student moves to the Regular Class, and record the decision. Movement is based on evidence, not on a family request.
tasks.timing_text: After six weeks, and again at the end of Term 1

source.quote: The Academic Coordinator reviews placement after six weeks and again at the end of Term 1 using real assessment results.

tasks.title: Complete the self-evaluation before your School Appraisal visit
tasks.description: With the Principal, update the Self-Evaluation Summary and evidence links in the Evidence Guide for all five domains. Without it the visit is rescheduled; during the visit you join the domain meetings.
tasks.timing_text: At least 5 working days before your school's Phase 1 visit (window 5 Aug–18 Sep) and Phase 3 visit (window 7 Oct–20 Nov)

source.quote: Before every scheduled on-site visit, schools must complete or update the Self-Evaluation Summary and working evidence links

tasks.title: Join the Phase 2 Progress Check-in with your Visit I Supervisor
tasks.description: The online check-in reviews self-appraisal progress across the five domains, the Phase 1 follow-up actions and your readiness for Phase 3. Have your updates ready in the Evidence Guide.
tasks.timing_text: On your school's Phase 2 date (4 September–16 October 2026); all check-ins are completed by 18 October

source.quote: The Visit I Supervisor schedules the Zoom meeting with the School Principal and Academic Coordinator.

tasks.title: Move the two School Development Priorities into your plan
tasks.description: With the Principal, carry the two priorities agreed in the Annual School Quality Report into the School Development Plan, with the related rubric aspects, ready for work in Semester II.
tasks.timing_text: Within two weeks of receiving your Annual School Quality Report (every school receives it by mid-December 2026)

source.quote: Steps 1–3 above, carrying forward the two agreed School Development Priorities and a short list of related rubric aspects

tasks.title: Take part in the Phase 4 Impact Review
tasks.description: Bring the evidence linked to the two School Development Priorities only: what was implemented, what changed and what should carry forward. It creates no new Domain Rating.
tasks.timing_text: Near the end of the year (May–June 2027, online)

source.quote: Participants: Principal, Academic Coordinator and relevant priority owners; led by the Visit I Supervisor with an Eduversal representative.

tasks.title: Chair the Assessment Committee meeting
tasks.description: Meet the Principal, all Heads of Department and the Learning Support Coordinator to review assessment data and student outcomes. For the June annual review, with Eduversal, compile the school-level assessment data for the self-study.
tasks.timing_text: August, November and February; June annual review (shown in the last teaching week so you can prepare)

source.quote: The Committee is chaired by the Academic Coordinator (AC) and comprises the School Principal, all Heads of Department (HoDs)

tasks.title: Get ready for the EASE Growth week
tasks.description: Confirm the grade-band day, rooms, devices and supervision, and remind staff that EASE Growth is not a curriculum test and lessons continue. Use the week to check pacing against plan.
tasks.timing_text: Before EASE Week 1 (28 Sep–2 Oct 2026) and EASE Week 3 (29 Mar–2 Apr 2027)

source.quote: Confirm rooms, devices, and the grade-band timetable; check pacing against plan

tasks.title: Follow up incidents and absences from the EASE Growth week
tasks.description: Collect any technical or administrative incidents, pass them to the Principal or the Academic Board as needed, and arrange make-ups under the same conditions within 5 working days where the school offers them.
tasks.timing_text: Straight after EASE Week 1 and EASE Week 3

source.quote: Record significant technical or administrative incidents and escalate them through the school Academic Coordinator.

tasks.title: Prepare the Synchronized Test week
tasks.description: Tell teachers and students the Synchronized Test dates, confirm invigilation and Latihan.id access, and remind staff that lessons stop for the week. Afterwards, collect the results for analysis and make sure they are in Edunav before the 19 December and 29 May reports.
tasks.timing_text: Before EASE Week 2 (7–11 Dec 2026) and EASE Week 4 (10–14 May 2027)

source.quote: Confirm the schedule, invigilation, and access; then collect results for analysis

tasks.title: Check Teacher-Paced Tests are completed within their windows
tasks.description: Look at this month's Teacher-Paced Test windows and make sure every class has sat its test before the window closes.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a month (windows follow the Annual Plan)

source.quote: Academic Coordinators at each school are responsible for ensuring students complete the test within the window.

tasks.title: Lead the moderation sample for recent Common Assessments
tasks.description: Where manual marking applies, sample 3–5 marked papers against the mark scheme and correct any pattern of inconsistent grading before results are final.
tasks.timing_text: After each EASE Assessment — suggested: check once a month

source.quote: The Academic Coordinator leads a moderation check, sampling 3–5 papers per school after each EASE Assessment.

tasks.title: Make sure assessment results are in Edunav before reports
tasks.description: Check that every Common Assessment result, online or on paper, is entered in Edunav in time for the midterm report cards.
tasks.timing_text: Before each midterm report distribution (17 October 2026 and 17 April 2027)

source.quote: Ensuring results are entered into Edunav on time.

tasks.title: Update the Curriculum Coverage Tracker
tasks.description: Review each subject's status (On Track, Watch, At Risk, Escalated) with the Heads of Department. An "At Risk" status needs a documented recovery action, never silently dropped content.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a month

source.quote: Curriculum coverage is reviewed by the Academic Coordinator.

tasks.title: Look for teachers who need support in observation data
tasks.description: Read the observation and walkthrough records together to see which teachers would benefit from support before their next observation.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a month

source.quote: Analyze classroom observation data and walkthrough data regularly to identify teachers who need support.

tasks.title: Check every teacher is on track for three formal observations
tasks.description: Without the minimum number of valid formal observations, F2 stays incomplete. Plan the missing ones now, avoiding the last day before a holiday and exam dates.
tasks.timing_text: A few weeks before each semester ends

source.quote: For F2, the school's own appraisers conduct at least three formal observations per semester (six or more per academic year)

tasks.title: Review the Semester I EASE Growth baseline results
tasks.description: When the School Baseline Summary is released, read it with the Principal and pick out students who need support. Version 1 is a baseline: never call a result "growth", rank classes or use it in appraisal.
tasks.timing_text: When the Semester I School Baseline Summary is released (the grade-band guides place this review in December)

source.quote: Academic Coordinator reviews EASE Growth Test results.

tasks.title: Write the Semester I results analysis
tasks.description: Read Common Assessment and EASE Growth patterns by subject and by class, check that students below KKTP got their reassessment within 10 working days, and end with a few clear decisions.
tasks.timing_text: End of Semester I, after EASE Week 2 (shown in the first week back)

source.quote: Semester I results analysis: Common Assessment and EASE Growth patterns, by subject and by class

tasks.title: Lead the year-end curriculum and results review
tasks.description: Complete the coverage audit, the transition readiness profiles for each grade band and the full-year results analysis, including the Semester II EASE Growth baseline (never described as growth). Turn them into next year's improvement priorities.
tasks.timing_text: May–June (after EASE Week 4; shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: Complete coverage audit, transition readiness profiles, results analysis, and next-year improvement priorities.

tasks.title: Collect Progression Test results and use them for planning
tasks.description: Make sure results reach school-level planning. The Stage 9 test is required for Checkpoint schools, about 4–6 weeks before Checkpoint; review it with the short intervention plan.
tasks.timing_text: After each stage is completed (Stage 8 around Sep–Oct, Stage 7 around January, Stage 9 before Checkpoint)

source.quote: The Academic Coordinator should ensure results are collected and used for school-level planning.

tasks.title: Confirm which subjects can run before counselling opens
tasks.description: Agree with the Heads of Department which IGCSE and AS Level subjects you can offer. Check the 10-student minimum, teacher availability and timetable clashes before students choose.
tasks.timing_text: Before the Semester II counselling window opens

source.quote: Confirm with your Heads of Department which subjects your school can realistically offer this year.

tasks.title: Support Grade 8 and Grade 10 subject-choice conversations
tasks.description: Use the selection forms and bring the evidence (Common Assessment, EASE Growth, Checkpoint) so student and family see the same picture. The goal is a good conversation, not a veto.
tasks.timing_text: Semester II counselling window: Grade 8 IGCSE and Grade 10 AS/A Level (AS counselling begins by March at the latest)

source.quote: Support the individual conversations where a student's choice looks like a poor fit.

tasks.title: Confirm final subject choices and tell families in writing
tasks.description: Agree final numbers with the Principal, settle the timetable, and send the confirmed subjects to families in writing.
tasks.timing_text: After your school's counselling window closes (suggested: April)

source.quote: Confirm final numbers with the Principal, finalize the timetabling implications, and communicate the confirmed subjects to families in writing.

tasks.title: Plan this semester's portfolio review and Student-Led Conference
tasks.description: If you are the school's Portfolio Coordinator, set the date, ideally inside an existing parent or reporting window, and check that the platform and teachers are ready.
tasks.timing_text: Once each semester, on dates your school sets

source.quote: two portfolio-led review/SLC cycles a year, one in each semester, on dates each school sets

tasks.title: Prepare End-of-Year Conferences for the teachers you appraise
tasks.description: The conference brings together the year's observation record, adds F3 Work Inspection and the annual Student Survey result, and finalises the teacher's appraisal record.
tasks.timing_text: Later in Semester II

source.quote: The End-of-Year Conference session, held later in Semester 2, retrieves the accumulated appraisal record

tasks.title: Review each Grade 11 student's portfolio draft
tasks.description: Go through the activity record with each Grade 11 student so the extracurricular profile is documented before Grade 12.
tasks.timing_text: May (Grade 11)

source.quote: Academic Coordinator reviews portfolio draft with student.

notes_for_reviewer: Overlap with the Principal file: the School Principals Checklist is addressed 'For principals and academic coordinators'. I took only one item from it (analyse observation and walkthrough data, AC2-028, 'recommended'). Its other academic items that match the AC's work (plan the EASE Assessment calendar, confirm the EASE Growth slot, check weekly teaching progress, review each Common Assessment cycle for consistency) are covered here from AC-specific documents instead (Induction: Academic Coordinators; EASE Assessment: Standards 6.1; EASE Principal's Guide §6). Please make sure the Principal file does not list the same duties, or decide who owns each one.

Left to the Cambridge Coordinator file: the checklist items on Cambridge entries, predicted grades, coursework moderation deadlines and 'After each exam series, analyze Cambridge results against predicted grades…'. The live documents do not clearly give these to the AC.

Semester-end timing: EASE Week 2 (7–11 Dec) and EASE Week 4 (10–14 May) fall after the last teaching week. So the Semester I results analysis (AC2-031) shows in the first week of Semester II, and the year-end review (AC2-032), Phase 4 (AC2-019) and the June Assessment Committee review (AC2-020, date 2027-06-01) fall back to the last teaching week (3–7 May) as preparation. timing_text says so.

Assessment Committee (AC2-020): Assessment Policy §14.3 fixes the meetings as August, November, February and June. The June annual review is after teaching ends, so it shows in the last teaching week.

Grade 10 Intensive review (AC2-015): the live text says 'after six weeks and again at the end of Term 1'. I read Term 1 as Semester I (24 Aug and 30 Nov 2026). Please confirm what 'Term 1' means in the grade-band documents.

External exams check (AC2-010): 'Before the start of Grade 11 counseling' is ambiguous (Grade 10 Semester II AS counselling, or the start of Grade 11). I placed it at the year start and again in January, before AS counselling. Please confirm.

Subject counselling (AC2-034 to AC2-036): the live documents give the Grade 10 AS window as Semester II, beginning 'by March at the latest' (Grades 09-10 Structure). For the Grade 8 IGCSE window they say only 'Grade 8, Semester II'. The January, February/March and April placements are suggestions.

End-of-Year Conference (AC2-038) is 'recommended': the Teacher Appraisal Handbook does not say which appraiser runs it, and the AC induction guide says the AC does not decide a teacher's final appraisal outcome (the Principal does).

EASE Growth: the release date of the School Baseline Summary is not in the live documents (it follows the Growth Team's technical checks). The Semester I review (AC2-030) is placed in the last teaching week because the grade-band guides say December. The Semester II review is folded into the year-end review (AC2-032) to keep the last week light.

Phase 2 Progress Check-in (AC2-017): the School Appraisal Overview table gives school dates from 4 Sep to 16 Oct 2026, so the task shows in the first teaching week of that window. The brief says only 'completed by 18 Oct'.

Grades 4–6 EASE Growth: the brief says 18–22 January 2027, but calendar-2026-27.txt says 17–21 January 2027. It is not used in this file, because the Curriculum Module (and the AC's work in it) covers Grades 7–12. The Principal file should check which date is right.

Title drift in the live pack: the Student Pathways & Subject Selection Guide has the page footer 'Curriculum Module: Career Pathways 26-27', and the AC induction guide calls it 'Curriculum Module: Cambridge Career Pathways 26-27'. I used the title from the export file name. The Career Growth Framework title ('Career Growth Framework 26-27') and the grade-band titles ('Curriculum Module: Grades 07-08 Structure' etc.) are also taken from the file names and page footers. Please confirm all three against Drive.

Induction: Academic Coordinators §3.3 asks who signs the semester results analysis 'before it goes to the school's leadership or to the yayasan'. This is not used here, but you may want to check that wording against the FR/GM line.

Left out because the live documents give no timing or do not clearly give it to the AC: the twice-yearly network Academic Coordinator training (no dates), Phase 0 Kickoff (AC attendance not stated), Stage 7/8 Progression Test timing beyond 'after stage completion', and Grade 11 tracking of AS preparation and English-test completion ('Track AS Level preparation and English test completion across the year', Grades 11-12 Structure), which could become a monthly task if you want it.
The portfolio task (AC2-037) applies only where the school names the AC as Portfolio Coordinator ('normally the Academic Coordinator, Cambridge Coordinator, Principal…'), so it is 'recommended'.

Load, simulated with my own reading of the `when` rules: 36 teaching weeks. The heaviest weeks are 13 Jul 2026 (7) and 3 May 2027 (7), then the first week of Semester II (6) and 30 Nov 2026 (5); most weeks have 0–4. Both monthly 'first' and 'last' tasks land on 3 May because May has only one teaching week. Please re-run with the real seeder.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A short regular review of an at-risk student list (students below KKTP, reassessments due, Tier 2 referrals).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The live documents require reteaching plus one reassessment within 10 working days and Tier 2 referral, but nobody is given a regular check that this is happening. The AC induction guide itself warns that a remedial process can quietly stop running.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A year-start briefing and calibration session on the F2 rubric and walkthroughs for the school's own appraisers.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The AC induction guide says the school's appraisers see each teacher six or more times 'but are not calibrated'; a short shared calibration would make the school-owned F2 score fairer.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A monthly check of walkthrough coverage: which teachers have had written walkthrough feedback in Edunav.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Walkthrough feedback must be shared in writing through Edunav, but no one checks coverage; it would also feed the observation-data review (AC2-028).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Teacher Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 / Teacher Appraisal: Walkthrough Form 26-27

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: An end-of-semester gradebook check before report cards: categories complete, weightings unchanged, remedial grades capped at KKTP.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The live documents only say results must be entered into Edunav on time; a short integrity check before 19 December and 29 May would protect report-card accuracy.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A mid-year check of teachers' growth areas and PD plans with the Subject Leaders.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Teacher Development Capacity-Building Guide gives this rhythm to the 'School Leader' but says the owner is 'usually the Academic Coordinator / School Principal'. Naming the AC's part would make the December review happen.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: An annual cross-grade-band gap analysis (Grade 8→9, 9→10, 10→11, 11→12) using coverage trackers and results.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Implementation Toolkit has Transition Readiness Profiles for each grade band, but no view across bands of topics that are weak year after year.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: An annual check that textbooks, Cambridge resources and digital platforms still match the current syllabus versions.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The checklist asks schools to confirm resources are available, but nothing checks that they still match updated syllabi before the next year.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Curriculum Module: Implementation Toolkit 26-27 (minimum evidence set)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A monthly developmental learning walk with Subject Leaders on one agreed teaching theme (no score).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: It gives the AC a regular, non-evaluative view across subjects, which the induction guide calls the core habit of the role.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Teaching & Learning: Observed Best Practices / Appraisal Suite: Network Peer Review 26-27
